interviewee.note: THE case the other two samples cannot exercise: the speaker is NAMED. She self-introduces ('My name's Alma Reyes') and the interviewer addresses her by title ('Thank you for sitting down with me, Ms. Reyes'), so interviewee_identity should resolve and the named PERSON should be folded into e000. Her gender is then provable deterministically from the interviewer's honorific, which is the only checker that can POSITIVELY support interviewee_gender -- in interviews 001 and 002 the speaker is never named, so it can never fire and the field is unverifiable in principle.

people.note: mother; the alias is introduced with a PRONOUN subject ('everybody on the block called her Pera'), so the merge depends on resolving 'her' to the nearest preceding person of matching gender rather than on a shared name token
daughter; owns the parish social-media handle, so that identifier must NOT be attributed to the speaker
public figure in PUBLIC_FIGURES, used impersonally ('Reagan was president when the layoffs started') -> keep. The keep still has to clear personal_signal_absent and not_kin_of_interviewee.

dates.note: the SPEAKER'S OWN date of birth -- the single most consequential field for interviewee-only surrogate generation
nationally known public event -> resolves from the anchor table, stays non-shiftable, and its phrase is kept: naming it identifies nobody

ages.note: the mother's age; 'She was ninety-one' -- a third-person subject governs the span, so it must not be attributed to the speaker
the father's; a decade expression, so approximate

locations.note: in the gazetteer with Illinois as its parent, and both are mentioned -> the one LOCATED_IN edge in this transcript
a street plus a birth date is a household

a Mexican state of ~6M people, so naming it singles out nobody. The pipeline OVER-REDACTS it, for the same reason it over-redacts Mekong Delta in 001: the gazetteer does not know it, no type word sits beside the mention, and keep_rests_on_a_verified_type refuses a keep built on an uncorroborated LLM type.
a named employer is a direct pointer to a person; an institution is never keepable

identifiers.note: two sentences after the binding first-person cue, with nothing intervening -> the bounded lookback in checks/ownership must reach it
the daughter's ('My daughter set up an account'): a kin noun stands between the cue and the span
